examples.en: I shifted the car's gear to third.

examples.ko: 자전거 기어가 고장 나서 수리점에 갔어요.
examples.en: The bicycle gear broke, so I went to the repair shop.
Shift to a lower gear when climbing a hill.

examples.ko: 시계 안에는 작은 기어가 많이 들어 있어요.
examples.en: A watch has many small gears inside.

examples.ko: 운전 연습을 하다가 기어를 잘못 넣었어요.
examples.en: While practicing driving, I put it in the wrong gear.
The gears mesh together and the machine turns.

explain: 기어는 자동차나 자전거에서 속도와 힘을 바꾸는 장치나 바퀴를 말해요. 자동차에서는 '기어를 넣다', '기어를 바꾸다'처럼 말해요. '기어가다'의 '기어'(기다+어)와 글자가 같아서 문장을 보고 구별해요.
explain_en: 기어 is a gear in a car or bicycle, the part that changes speed and force. For cars you say '기어를 넣다' or '기어를 바꾸다'. The verb form '기어' (from 기다, to crawl, as in 기어가다) is written the same, so check the sentence to tell them apart.

examples.en: It's the tail end of winter, so mornings are still cold.
I met my friend at the far end of the alley.
The closing part of that movie is moving.
I walked holding the hem of my skirt.
It rained at the very end of my vacation.
There is a small village at the foot of the mountain.

explain: 그냥 '끝'보다 천천히 끝나 가는 부분이라는 느낌이 있어요. 계절과 휴가 같은 때에는 '가을의 끝자락'처럼, 옷과 골목 같은 곳에는 '치마 끝자락'처럼 써요. '마지막'은 딱 하나뿐인 맨 뒤를 말해요.
explain_en: It feels like a part that is slowly ending, rather than a plain 끝 (end). It works for times, as in '가을의 끝자락' (the tail end of autumn), and for places or things like '치마 끝자락' (hem of a skirt). 마지막 means the very last one.

dis.h: Very last edge or tail of a period or place

p.n: 끝 is a plain end point; 끝자락 means the fading tail part.

examples.en: The company stores customer information in a database.
The database broke down, so the site stopped.

examples.ko: 이 앱은 단어를 데이터베이스에서 찾아 보여 줘요.
examples.en: This app finds words in a database and shows them.
I am learning how to build a database.

examples.ko: 새 데이터베이스로 옮기는 데 하루가 걸렸어요.
examples.en: Moving to the new database took a day.
I searched for papers in the library database.

explain: 'DB'라고 줄여 쓰고, 말로는 '디비'라고 읽어요. 보통 '데이터베이스에 저장하다', '데이터베이스에서 찾다'처럼 에/에서와 함께 써요.
explain_en: It is shortened to 'DB' in writing and read aloud as '디비'. It usually appears with the particles 에/에서, as in '데이터베이스에 저장하다' (save to the database) and '데이터베이스에서 찾다' (search in the database).

examples.ko: 감기 때문에 사나흘 동안 학교에 못 갔어요.
examples.en: I couldn't go to school for three or four days because of a cold.
I'm planning to go on a trip for three or four days.

examples.ko: 이 김치는 사나흘 뒤에 먹으면 맛있어요.
examples.en: This kimchi tastes good after three or four days.
It has been raining for three or four days straight.
The item you ordered will arrive in three or four days.

examples.ko: 일이 많아서 사나흘은 밤을 새워야 해요.
examples.en: I have so much work that I'll need to stay up nights for three or four days.

explain: 사흘이나 나흘쯤 되는 기간을 대충 말할 때 써요. 정확한 숫자보다 '대략 그 정도'라는 느낌이라서 일정이나 기간을 말할 때 편해요. 같은 느낌으로 '이삼일', '삼사일'이라고도 해요.
explain_en: It refers to a period of roughly three or four days, so it feels approximate rather than exact, which is handy for schedules. '이삼일' and '삼사일' give a similar feel.

examples.ko: 오늘은 여느 날과 다르게 일찍 일어났어요.
examples.en: Today I woke up early, unlike any usual day.
I had coffee and went to work as usual.

examples.ko: 그 집 음식은 여느 식당보다 맛있어요.
examples.en: That place's food tastes better than at an ordinary restaurant.
Like any other kid, he likes comics.
This winter is colder than an average year.
That day started just like any other weekend.

explain: '여느'는 항상 뒤에 명사가 와요. '여느 때/날/사람'처럼 쓰고 보통 '~와 다르다', '~처럼', '~보다'가 따라와요. '다른'은 서로 같지 않다는 뜻이고 '여느'는 '평범한'이라는 뜻이라 헷갈리지 않게 주의하세요.
explain_en: '여느' must always be followed by a noun, as in '여느 때', '여느 날' and '여느 사람', and is usually followed by '~와 다르다', '~처럼' or '~보다'. '다른' means not the same, but '여느' means ordinary, so be careful not to mix them up.

examples.en: It's market day, so there's a lot to see at the market.

examples.ko: 우리 동네는 오 일에 한 번 장날이 서요.
examples.en: In our town, market day comes once every five days.
Grandma goes out to sell vegetables every market day.

examples.ko: 장날에 가면 싱싱한 나물을 싸게 살 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you go on market day, you can buy fresh greens cheaply.
Do you know when the next market day is?
Today is market day, so the roads are really jammed.

explain: 오일장처럼 정해진 날에 열리는 시장이 서는 날이에요. 요즘 도시에서는 매일 가게가 열려서 시골이나 전통 시장 이야기에서 많이 나와요.

phrases.example: 오랜만에 그 식당에 갔는데 가는 날이 장날이라고 문을 닫았더라고요.
phrases.en: I went to that restaurant for the first time in a while, and just my luck, it was closed.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일이 있어서 갔더니 공교롭게도 일이 꼬였을 때 쓰는 속담이에요. 보통 운이 나쁘거나 타이밍이 안 맞았을 때 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A proverb for when you go somewhere and things unluckily turn out wrong. It is mostly said about bad luck or bad timing.

explain_en: It is the day a periodic market, like a five-day market, is held. Because city shops open every day, it appears mostly in talk about the countryside and traditional markets.

examples.en: I made a flower shape with wire.
The wire is bent, so it's hard to straighten.
We put up a wire fence in the garden.
I put on gloves and held the wire carefully.
My clothes tore after catching on a wire.
This wire is thin, so it breaks easily.

explain: '전선'은 전기가 흐르는 줄이고, '철사'는 모양을 잡거나 묶을 때 쓰는 금속 줄이에요. 꽃가게나 만들기 수업에서 자주 써요.
explain_en: 전선 is a cable that carries electricity, while 철사 is a metal wire used to shape or tie things. It is often used in flower shops and craft classes.

examples.en: The ship leaves port at seven in the morning.

examples.ko: 태풍 때문에 어제는 배가 출항하지 못했어요.
examples.en: Because of the typhoon, the ship could not leave port yesterday.
The fishermen set out to sea at dawn.
I waved at the ship that was leaving port.
If the weather clears up, we will set sail tomorrow.
The cruise ship leaves port in Busan and goes to Japan.

explain: '출항하다'는 배에만 써요. 비행기가 떠날 때는 '이륙하다', 버스나 기차는 '출발하다'를 써요. 반대로 배가 항구에 들어오는 것은 '입항하다'예요.
explain_en: '출항하다' is used only for ships. A plane taking off is '이륙하다', and buses and trains use '출발하다'. The opposite, a ship entering a harbor, is '입항하다'.

dis.h: a ship leaves port to sail

p.n: 출발하다 is general; 출항하다 is only for ships leaving port.
